input.quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
input.rationale: An insurance covenant exists (Section 14): workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1M, E&O of USD 1M, plus certificates and notice of material change on Company request. That satisfies the workers' comp, CGL and certificate elements and the fallback E&O level, but it contains no cyber/privacy cover at all, and the fallback requires cyber of at least USD 2M. Contractor's personnel work at Company facilities, access Company computer systems and handle Confidential Information including Company records and information, so cyber cover is material rather than a minor sub-element. Minimal fix: add cyber liability (privacy/data breach) at USD 2,000,000 into the existing list, i.e. the fallback level, since the existing bargain is set at USD 1M coverages and the preferred USD 5M cyber (and USD 2M E&O / USD 2M CGL aggregate) would be disproportionate for this consulting scope; the shortfall against those preferred limits is noted but not pressed.

proposal.summary: Add cyber/privacy liability insurance (USD 2M) to Contractor's insurance covenant
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Contractor accesses our systems and Confidential Information, so we have added cyber/privacy liability cover at USD 2,000,000 alongside the existing coverages; our preferred position is USD 5,000,000 where Company data is processed, but we are content with USD 2,000,000 given the scope of the Services.
